content:
Something under central Laredo gave way around 3 a.m. Tuesday. According to KGNS, a street caved in near Barcelona Avenue and West Frost Street, and a large amount of water began flowing from the site — enough to block the Valencia side of the road. Laredo police officers responded and are warning drivers to avoid the area.

Here is what the morning's reporting does not tell us: where the water is coming from. KGNS reports that the source of the water is unknown. There is no word yet on injuries, no statement from the city on what caused the collapse, and no detour information for drivers who use that corridor in central Laredo.

That is a lot of unknowns for a story about a hole opening in a public street — and it is not happening in a vacuum. Just yesterday, lanes reopened after a waterline break at McPherson Avenue and Taylor Street. That makes two water-related street incidents in two days, in different parts of the city. One waterline break is an incident. Two in two days starts to look like a pattern — the kind of pattern that makes residents ask reasonable questions about the condition of the pipes under their feet.

Laredo's water infrastructure is not new, and it is not cheap to fix. What is cheap is transparency: telling residents quickly what broke, why it broke, and when the street will be safe to drive on again. As of early Tuesday morning, none of that had been said publicly about the Barcelona Avenue collapse.

Webb Watch 956 will be asking the questions the morning rush deserves answers to:

  • What caused the street to cave in — a water main break, a sewer collapse, or something else?
  • Was this section of road or the infrastructure beneath it flagged for repairs before Tuesday?
  • How long will the closure last, and what is the detour for commuters?
  • Are these two water incidents in two days connected — and does the city know the age and condition of the lines beneath central Laredo?

Drivers should take the police warning seriously and stay out of the area until the city has said the road is clear. We will update this story as the city releases information — if it does.

Sources: KGNS, "Street caves in near central Laredo, water flowing blocks road," Oct. 20, 2026.

title: A Street Caved In Near Barcelona Avenue This Morning — and Nobody Knows Where the Water Is Coming From
